# Interviews

This is the **Interviews** top-level category of the Knowledge Library. It will become a coherent English-language book built around the interview preparation materials you upload.

**The source material comes first.** No book has been assigned to this section yet, so we will not invent chapter content, claim that a particular book has been studied, or create hundreds of empty pages.

## How we will build the book

1. **Read the actual source.** Identify its title, edition, table of contents, chapter goals and examples. If an uploaded PDF is a preview, explicitly note what it does and does not contain.
2. **Design a learning path.** Organise related topics by prerequisite knowledge and difficulty. Retain the book's terminology and sequence where useful, and distinguish different books' perspectives.
3. **Write substantial chapters.** Each question begins with a concrete problem, develops the simplest viable model, explains the underlying principle, and ends with an interview-ready answer.
4. **Show the reasoning.** When mathematics is helpful, every formula must immediately define its symbols, substitute actual numbers and justify the conclusion. Where appropriate, use a very small runnable program.
5. **Practise speaking.** After understanding the material, rehearse a concise explanation, a deeper follow-up and common interviewer challenges. Memorising a script is not the goal.
6. **Check the source and examples.** Attribute each source, independently verify the numerical/programming examples and distinguish book material from new illustrative material.

## Tips & Notes

[**Interview Tips & Notes**](tips-and-notes/index.qmd) is the first second-level section. It contains concise, independently written advice on structuring technical answers, explaining trade-offs, and handling challenging follow-up questions. It is available now; future book-based topic sections will be added after you upload their sources.

## Planned study formats

As the uploaded books establish the scope, each developed topic can contain:

- **Concept chapter** — explanations, derivations and examples.
- **Classic interview question** — the exact question, requirements and assumptions as supported by the source.
- **Follow-up challenges** — modifications that test whether the principle is understood.
- **Spoken answer** — a natural British-English answer suitable for interview practice.
- **Source map** — book edition, chapter or page number, plus where the topic belongs in this library.

These are **formats**, not a claim that a particular technical subject has already been covered. We will add subcategories only after inspecting the supplied books.

## Related existing study material

Some interview-relevant material already lives in [Algorithms](../algorithms/index.qmd), [System Design](../system-design/index.qmd), [Programming Languages](../programming-languages/index.qmd) and [Mathematics](../mathematics/index.qmd). Those are independent knowledge courses. This new **Interviews** section will be the separate, source-led practice book rather than duplicating their content without a reason.

Read the [interview book authoring guide](reading-and-authoring-guide.qmd) for the standards used when new books arrive.
